the_finding: ⛔ THE RED WAS THE SMALL HALF. `research/modalities/atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json` is ONE FILENAME THAT HAS HELD TWO DIFFERENT GEO SERIES, and two modules read it as two different things. From committed history, not inference (git log over that path, after unshallowing the clone): 2026-08-05 it held GSE299349, the series its producer atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py declares in `SERIES`; 325258cb8 on 2026-08-07 17:27 UTC overwrote it with GSE28866, 99 samples, because emc-expression-datasets.yml mode=gse-series passes a free `series` input to a module whose output path is FIXED; emc_cohort_search.py and its committed verdict were then written on 2026-08-08 AGAINST that GSE28866 content; a8caba9 on 2026-08-27 04:37 UTC re-fetched GSE299349 to repair PUB-ATR §8 (CYC-0016, correctly) and took the 3SEQ arm with it. Both readers were right about a filename that could only be right for one of them. ⭐ THE DAMAGE WAS NOT THE THREE RED TESTS. `_known_gsms()` is dedup level 3 of the guard that stops a re-deposit of a cohort the manuscript already reads being counted as a FOURTH EMC cohort — the GSE170983/GSE28866 trap emc_cohort_search.py exists to catch. It fell from 157 GSMs to 126 (58 fusion-target + 99 Brunner → 58 + 68 unrelated), lost every GSE28866 GSM, and labelled 68 BCOR-rearranged sarcoma CELL-LINE samples with the string 'GSE299349 = GSE170983, the Brunner deposit (the 3SEQ arm)'. A re-deposit sharing neither accession nor PMID graded NEW_CANDIDATE. It degraded silently because the read was wrapped in `if os.path.exists(...)` and took the series identifier from whatever it found — an absent reading rendered as a reading of absence, which is the failure this module's own docstring names.

process_defect_found_in_this_cycle.what: ⛔ A MUTATION HARNESS THAT EXERCISES A WRITING CODE PATH DAMAGES THE TREE, AND THIS ONE REPRODUCED THE VERY INCIDENT IT WAS TESTING THE FIX FOR. The first version of the refusal test called `main(['--fetch', '--series', 'GSE28866'])` and relied on the guard to stop before the fetch. That is the right assertion and the wrong mechanics: mutation M6 removed the guard, the real fetch half ran, and because that half RECORDS failures rather than raising, it derived and WROTE — putting series GSE28866 into atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json and its inputs cache at 2026-08-27T05:20:09Z. That is exactly the clobber this cycle exists to close, performed by the test for the fix. Measured, not theorised: `git status` showed both artifacts modified and `json.load(...)['series']` read 'GSE28866'.
process_defect_found_in_this_cycle.how_it_was_caught: The harness's own post-restore run. It restores the source and re-runs, and that run came back '1 failed, 11 passed' against a green pre-mutation baseline. Without that step the damage would have been committed inside a commit whose subject is 'stop this file being overwritten'.
process_defect_found_in_this_cycle.fix_applied: Both artifacts restored with `git checkout --` (they were committed and untouched at HEAD, so nothing was lost), and the test now monkeypatches `M.fetch` to raise. The assertion is now about ORDER — refuse before anything reaches the network or the writer — and a violation fails loudly instead of quietly. Side effect worth having: the three mutations went from 169 s each to 0.2 s.
process_defect_found_in_this_cycle.the_general_rule: A mutation removes a guard by construction, so every code path that guard was protecting WILL run. Stub the destructive half before mutating, and always re-run clean after restoring.
